title: New Hope for Breast Cancer Patients as NHS Approves Life-Extending Drug
subtitle: After years of campaigning, women in England gain access to a treatment that provides vital extra time with their families.

summary.en: Patients in England with a specific type of incurable breast cancer can now receive the drug Enhertu through the NHS. The decision follows two years of intense campaigning after the drug was previously rejected for being too expensive. Clinical trials show that the treatment can extend life by several months for those with HER2-low breast cancer. While charities celebrate the news, they also highlight the sadness of those who did not live to see this change. The government and drug companies reached a new agreement to make the medicine available to about 1,000 women each year.
summary.zh: 英格蘭患有特定類型無法治癒乳癌的病患，現在可以透過 NHS 取得 Enhertu 藥物。這項決定是在該藥物先前因價格過高被拒絕後，經過兩年強烈爭取才達成的。臨床試驗顯示，該治療能為 HER2 低表現型乳癌患者延長數個月的壽命。雖然慈善機構對此消息表示慶祝，但也強調了那些沒能等到這項變革的逝者所帶來的遺憾。政府與藥廠達成了一項新協議，使每年約 1,000 名女性能夠獲得此藥物治療。

paragraphs.en: Thousands of women in England living with a specific form of incurable breast cancer have received life-changing news. Starting this week, the National Health Service (NHS) will provide a drug called Enhertu to patients with HER2-low advanced breast cancer. This decision marks the end of a long and difficult two-year wait for many families, as the treatment was previously rejected by the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) because it was considered too expensive.
paragraphs.zh: 數千名居住在英格蘭、患有特定類型無法治癒乳癌的女性，收到了一個足以改變人生的消息。從本週開始，英國國家醫療保健服務（NHS）將為「HER2低表現型」晚期乳癌患者提供一種名為「Enhertu」的藥物。這項決定終結了許多家庭長達兩年艱難且漫長的等待，因為該治療方案先前曾被英國國家健康與照顧卓越研究院（NICE）以價格過高為由拒絕。

paragraphs.en: NICE is the organization that advises the NHS on whether medical treatments offer good value for money. In July 2024, they decided that the cost of Enhertu was too high to justify its use. However, after persistent campaigning from charities, doctors, and patients, the government and the drug’s makers—AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo—returned to the negotiating table. According to The Guardian, the breakthrough came after a change in policy allowed the NHS to spend more on individual patient treatments, raising the limit from £30,000 to £35,000 per year.
paragraphs.zh: NICE 是負責建議 NHS 醫療處置是否具備成本效益的機構。在 2024 年 7 月，他們認定 Enhertu 的成本過高，無法支持其使用。然而，在慈善機構、醫師與病患持續奔走呼籲下，政府與該藥物的製造商——阿斯特捷利康（AstraZeneca）與第一三共（Daiichi Sankyo）——重回談判桌。根據《衛報》報導，這項突破源於政策的調整，允許 NHS 增加對個別病患治療的支出，將每年的上限從 3 萬英鎊提高至 3 萬 5 千英鎊。

paragraphs.en: For many, this news brings a mix of relief and deep sadness. Kate Wills, a 51-year-old mother living with stage four cancer, told the BBC that the news gave her "enormous hope." She explained that she now dares to dream of seeing her children grow up, get married, and fall in love. Yet, she also noted that the moment is bittersweet, as she thinks of friends who did not survive long enough to receive the treatment. Claire Rowney, chief executive of the charity Breast Cancer Now, echoed these feelings. While she called the decision a "milestone victory," she also stated that the country cannot celebrate without remembering the "devastating cost" of the two-year delay.
paragraphs.zh: 對許多人來說，這則消息帶來了如釋重負與深沉悲傷交織的複雜情緒。現年 51 歲、罹患第四期癌症的母親凱特·威爾斯（Kate Wills）告訴 BBC，這則消息給了她「巨大的希望」。她解釋說，現在她敢於夢想看著孩子長大、結婚並墜入愛河。然而，她也提到此刻心情苦樂參半，因為她想起了那些沒能撐到接受治療就離世的朋友。慈善機構「乳癌現在」（Breast Cancer Now）執行長克萊兒·羅尼（Claire Rowney）也呼應了這些感受。雖然她稱這項決定為「里程碑式的勝利」，但她也表示，國家在慶祝的同時，不能忘記這兩年延宕所帶來的「毀滅性代價」。

paragraphs.en: Enhertu is a targeted treatment that works differently than standard chemotherapy. Dr. Catherine Elliott, a director at Cancer Research UK, explained that the drug delivers medicine directly to cancer cells. Clinical trials have shown that this approach is highly effective. For patients with HER2-low advanced breast cancer, the drug can help them live longer and slow the progress of the disease. On average, patients using Enhertu gained about 6.6 months of extra life compared to those using standard treatments, with some individuals living up to three years longer.
paragraphs.zh: Enhertu 是一種標靶治療藥物，其運作方式與標準化學治療不同。英國癌症研究協會（Cancer Research UK）的主管凱瑟琳·艾略特（Catherine Elliott）博士解釋說，該藥物能將藥效直接送達癌細胞。臨床試驗顯示，這種方法極為有效。對於 HER2 低表現型晚期乳癌患者而言，該藥物能幫助她們延長壽命並減緩疾病惡化。平均而言，使用 Enhertu 的患者相較於使用標準治療的患者，能多出約 6.6 個月的生命，部分患者甚至能多存活長達三年。

paragraphs.en: This change brings England in line with other parts of the United Kingdom and Europe. Patients in Scotland have had access to the drug since 2023, and it is currently available in 26 other European countries. Following the announcement, officials indicated that doctors in Northern Ireland can now prescribe the drug, and Wales is expected to follow the same path shortly. Health Secretary Yvette Cooper praised the efforts of the campaigners, stating that the recommendation is a "tribute" to the charities that never stopped fighting for access.
paragraphs.zh: 這項變革使英格蘭與英國其他地區及歐洲同步。蘇格蘭的病患自 2023 年起便能取得該藥物，目前該藥物也已在其他 26 個歐洲國家上市。消息宣布後，官員表示北愛爾蘭的醫師現在可以開立此藥，威爾斯預計也將在不久後跟進。英國衛生大臣伊薇特·庫柏（Yvette Cooper）讚揚了倡議人士的努力，並表示這項建議是對那些從未放棄爭取治療權利的慈善機構的「致敬」。

paragraphs.en: Despite the success of the new deal, questions remain about how the agreement was reached. The BBC reported that the drug companies did not significantly lower their prices during the negotiations. Instead, the reversal by NICE was largely made possible by a new financial arrangement involving the UK government and the United States. This "commercial solution" allowed the NHS to finally add the drug to its list of approved treatments.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管這項新協議取得成功，但關於協議如何達成仍存在疑問。BBC 報導指出，藥廠在談判過程中並未大幅調降價格。相反地，NICE 的立場逆轉主要歸功於英國政府與美國之間達成的一項新財務安排。這項「商業解決方案」讓 NHS 最終得以將該藥物納入核准治療清單中。

paragraphs.en: For the approximately 1,000 women in England who will benefit from this decision each year, the impact is profound. While the journey to this point was long and often painful, the availability of Enhertu provides a new, essential option for those facing the most difficult health challenges. As Dr. Anne Rigg, an NHS national advisor, noted, this is "hugely positive news" for women who will now have the opportunity to gain precious time with their loved ones.
paragraphs.zh: 對於每年在英格蘭將從這項決定中受益的約 1,000 名女性來說，影響極為深遠。雖然走到這一步的過程漫長且往往令人痛苦，但 Enhertu 的取得為那些面臨最艱鉅健康挑戰的人們提供了一個全新的關鍵選擇。正如 NHS 國家顧問安妮·里格（Anne Rigg）博士所言，這對那些現在有機會與摯愛共度寶貴時光的女性來說，是「極為正面的消息」。

keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（桌子），這裡用於固定搭配「negotiating table」。文中：the government and the drug’s makers—AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo—returned to the negotiating table.

quiz.question: What was the primary reason the NHS was finally able to approve the use of Enhertu?

options.A: The drug manufacturers significantly reduced the price of the medication.
options.B: The government increased the annual spending limit per patient for medical treatments.
options.C: The NICE organization determined that the drug was no longer considered expensive.
options.D: Clinical trials proved that the drug could cure the cancer completely.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，突破點在於政策變更，允許 NHS 將每位病患的年度治療預算上限從 30,000 英鎊提高至 35,000 英鎊。選項 A 錯誤，因為第六段明確指出藥廠並未顯著降價。選項 C 錯誤，因為 NICE 的立場改變是因為財務安排與預算調整，而非藥物本身變便宜。選項 D 錯誤，文章僅提到藥物能延長生命，並未稱其能「治癒」癌症。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why might the approval of Enhertu be described as 'bittersweet'?

options.A: Because the drug is only effective for a very small percentage of patients.
options.B: Because the government had to cut funding for other health services to afford it.
options.C: Because the long delay meant that some patients passed away before they could access the drug.
options.D: Because the drug has severe side effects that make the extra time less enjoyable.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第三段，Kate Wills 與 Claire Rowney 的發言指出，雖然這是一個勝利，但人們無法忽視兩年延遲所帶來的「毀滅性代價」，因為許多病友沒能活到藥物獲准的這一刻。選項 A 文章未提及；選項 B 屬於過度推論，文章未提到其他服務被削減；選項 D 文章中並未討論藥物的副作用，僅強調其有效性。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the word 'profound' mean as used in the context: 'the impact is profound'?

options.B: Very great or intense in effect.
options.C: Related to medical or scientific research.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在文中，「profound」用來形容藥物獲准對病患產生的影響，意指影響非常深遠、巨大且具備重大的生命意義。選項 A 指的是複雜難懂，不符合語境；選項 C 與醫學研究無直接關聯；選項 D 錯誤，因為這是一個長達兩年的漫長過程，並非短時間內發生。

quiz.question: What is the central message of this article?

options.A: A detailed analysis of how Enhertu works compared to standard chemotherapy.
options.B: A critique of the pharmaceutical companies for their high pricing strategies.
options.C: The history of breast cancer treatment policies within the United Kingdom.
options.D: The successful, yet delayed, approval of a life-extending drug for English breast cancer patients.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。本文主旨圍繞在 Enhertu 這款藥物終於在英國獲准使用，報導了這項決策的背景、對病患的意義，以及過程中經歷的漫長等待與政策角力。選項 A 只是文章中的一個小細節；選項 B 雖有提及藥廠，但並非文章核心；選項 C 範圍過大，文章專注於此特定藥物的個案，而非英國整體的癌症治療政策史。
